newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains head for parched Brazil soybean states - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Rains head for parched Brazil soybean states - Somar.

text.p: Rains were heading for Brazil's drought-stricken Rio Grande do Sul state while soil moisture remained normal in most of the other key soybean growing areas, said independent meteorologists Somar.
Two cold fronts were seen crossing the south in the next few days. The first will bring light rains to Rio Grande do Sul between January 13 and 14.
"The second will reach the state at the end of the week, causing a rise in cloud cover and bringing generalised rains to the soybean region," Somar said in its weekly report.
Showers will maintain soil moisture levels normal in the north and north-east of the key growing state of Parana, benefiting the area's soybean crop.
In the centre-west isolated showers, typical of the summer, will also create good soil moisture conditions.
Somar said rainfall had been very scarce in Rio Grande do Sul since the start of the month.

"Drought persists in the majority of soybean areas in the southern region and is starting to damage the crop, mainly in Rio Grande do Sul where the soil is suffering from a lack of moisture," it said.

A weather system was locking humidity from the Amazon in the south-east and centre-west so that cold fronts were having little effect on the south, only meeting the right conditions for rain once they reached the south-east.
